inspection_summary: Inspected all 429 normalized lines. The paper defines a coefficient-nondegenerate class of good Dirichlet series, proves short-window pole existence for good quotients built from shifted zeta-type factors, and organizes the contradiction through zero-avoiding Ingham lines, two maximum-modulus propagations with decaying kernels, and a mean-square lower bound forced by a non-small Dirichlet coefficient. The prose makes that architecture recoverable, but many displayed formulas and some region/exponent symbols are damaged by extraction; exact inequalities and quotient layouts are therefore quarantined pending scan verification.

sections_inspected.label: Abstract, introduction, and good-series definition
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States pole-abundance and pole-gap aims, compares the paper with the earlier restricted treatment, and introduces the coefficient nondegeneracy condition used by the mean-value argument.

sections_inspected.label: Theorem 1 and its extension remarks
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the concrete shifted-zeta quotient result, finite-sum closure under goodness, extensions to derivatives and several L-function families, effectivity, and localization.

sections_inspected.label: Notation and general short-window pole theorem
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Packages analytic continuation, zero-free, size, and parameter assumptions for a general good quotient and sets up proof by contradiction.

sections_inspected.label: Step I: Ingham lines
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses local zero counts and pigeonhole separation to choose horizontal lines on which logarithmic derivatives and the quotient are controlled.

sections_inspected.label: Step II: maximum modulus with decaying kernels
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Applies the maximum-modulus principle twice, first to obtain a uniform interior bound and then to propagate it to a left vertical line by balancing an auxiliary exponential weight.

sections_inspected.label: Step III: mean-value theorem and coefficient lower bound
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Quotes a Balasubramanian-Ramachandra mean-square lower bound, specializes it, and uses goodness to force a point where the quotient is large on the left line.

sections_inspected.label: Step IV: final contradiction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Compares the Step II upper bound with the Step III lower bound to contradict a sufficiently long pole-free interval.

sections_inspected.label: Concluding generalization and Theorem 3
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Describes a degree-dominance frontier for ray-class zeta products and states a purely imaginary shift specialization with logarithmic-logarithmic pole proximity.

sections_inspected.label: Acknowledgements, references, and author matter
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Non-mathematical end matter inspected for completeness; it contributes provenance but no depth unit.

accepted_units.title: Pole abundance and gap control beyond the earlier explicit-formula restrictions
accepted_units.why_material: The abstract and introduction identify the target phenomenon: a good quotient of products of zeta translates has infinitely many poles to the right of every fixed vertical threshold, with control of gaps between pole ordinates. They also say the treatment subsumes the earlier section without assuming RH and covers more functions, locating the paper's actual advance.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the paper's own scope claim and comparison with its predecessor, not an independent verification of the result.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The claim is recoverable from prose. Control-character damage affects words and the real-part symbol at line 12, but not the stated pole/gap objective.

accepted_units.title: A good Dirichlet series combines right-half-plane convergence with recurrent non-small coefficients
accepted_units.why_material: The definition couples convergence in a far right half-plane to a lower-bound condition asserting that sufficiently large multiplicative ranges contain a coefficient that is not too small. That coefficient condition is later the bridge from analytic mean values back to the Dirichlet series, while Remark 2 identifies it with the earlier paper's working hypothesis.
accepted_units.context_note: Lines 34-35 note that coefficients and the convergence parameter can depend on a localization parameter, although that variant is not developed here.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The semantic role of recurrent coefficient nondegeneracy is confirmed by lines 319-321, but the exact maximum range and exponent in lines 31-32 are extraction-damaged and require scan verification before exact reuse.

accepted_units.title: Good shifted-zeta quotients and finite sums have poles in every logarithmic ordinate window
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 1 turns the abstract goodness condition into a pole theorem for a Dirichlet polynomial times a quotient of finite products of shifted zeta functions. Besides infinitely many poles beyond each fixed ordinate threshold, it asserts a pole in an interval beginning at every sufficiently large Y and having logarithmic length, and preserves the conclusion for finite sums when the sum itself is good.
accepted_units.context_note: Lines 49-52 preview the proof architecture: estimates on Ingham lines, two kernel-weighted maximum-modulus applications, and a Balasubramanian-Ramachandra theorem. This unit overlaps immutable v1 unit full_openalex_w963283010_u01 but does not replace it.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The factor-product display at lines 53-68 is visibly damaged, so exact multiplicities, symbols, and numerator/denominator typography require scan verification; the surrounding prose and F=F1/F2 description support the quotient-level claim.

accepted_units.title: The pole mechanism extends across derivatives, ordinary and number-field L-functions, and localized shifts
accepted_units.why_material: The remarks separate what the proof actually needs from the initial zeta notation: bounded-order derivatives may replace numerator factors, ordinary L-functions and arithmetic-progression series may be used, number-field and ray-class zeta functions are admitted under a degree comparison, and shifts can vary under localization. This exposes a reusable analytic mechanism rather than a one-function accident.
accepted_units.context_note: The text says the number-field extension replaces the count comparison by a degree comparison and defers more general results to paper IV; it also records effectivity of constants and parameter dependence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Function names and degree inequalities are mostly readable in prose, but several Greek letters and product symbols are extraction-damaged. Exact replacement recipes should be checked against the scan before formal transcription.

accepted_units.title: Analytic control plus goodness forces a pole in a prescribed short vertical window
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 2 abstracts the concrete zeta quotient into F=F1/F2. Under analytic continuation, boundedness, a zero-free denominator, growth control, and scale conditions on H and auxiliary parameters, goodness rules out analyticity throughout the window T-H to T+H. This is the engine from which Theorem 1 is said to follow.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof assumes the theorem false only after the preliminary Ingham-line bounds, a sequencing distinction made explicitly at lines 180-181.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several half-plane boundaries, exponents, and parameter names in conditions (A)-(D) are damaged at lines 107-133. The qualitative hypothesis structure and conclusion are recoverable, but the exact theorem statement is scan-dependent.

accepted_units.title: Local zero counts produce zero-separated Ingham lines
accepted_units.why_material: Step I first bounds the number of denominator zeros in unit-height intervals and then applies pigeonhole separation to choose a horizontal line a controlled distance from every such zero. This converts a discrete zero count into a contour on which later analytic estimates can safely run.
accepted_units.context_note: The zero-count proof is cited to earlier work rather than reproduced, while the line-selection inference is stated directly.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The separation scale is readable as a reciprocal expression involving g and log of the auxiliary parameter, though the parameter glyph is imperfect; exact constants are not supplied in the source.

accepted_units.title: Zero separation controls the logarithmic derivative and then the quotient on horizontal boundaries
accepted_units.why_material: Lemmas 4.3-4.4 use an Ingham line to bound F2'/F2, integrate that information into a bound for log F2 and its reciprocal, and combine it with the numerator bound to control F. This is the analytic transfer that makes the selected horizontal contours usable in maximum-modulus rectangles.
accepted_units.context_note: The text emphasizes that these estimates precede the contradiction assumption; only after they are available does the proof assume no pole in the target region.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The quotient F2'/F2 and the direction of the ensuing bounds are recoverable, but exact powers in lines 157-175 contain layout damage and need scan verification for quantitative reuse.

accepted_units.title: A doubly decaying sine kernel turns contour bounds into an interior strip bound
accepted_units.why_material: The first maximum-modulus step multiplies F by an exponential of a squared sine. On a rectangle whose horizontal sides are Ingham lines, the kernel suppresses the potentially large horizontal-boundary contribution, while the two vertical sides have controlled values. The result is a uniform bound after trimming controlled neighborhoods of the vertical window's ends.
accepted_units.context_note: Lemma 5.1 supplies the kernel's boundedness near the real direction and double-exponential decay in the imaginary direction; Lemma 5.2 applies it with horizontal sides chosen just inside T plus or minus H.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The prose establishes the contour argument and decay role. The exact kernel scaling and the exponent of the resulting bound are broken across lines 185-206 and must be verified from the scan.

accepted_units.title: A second kernel and a balancing monomial transport the upper bound to a left vertical line
accepted_units.why_material: The second maximum-modulus step introduces Y(s)=F(s) times a power weight and another decaying sine kernel on a rectangle extending from a left line to the convergence half-plane. The power base is chosen to balance the two vertical-boundary contributions, and a sufficiently tall rectangle makes the horizontal contributions negligible, yielding a left-line upper bound.
accepted_units.context_note: This step is distinct from Lemma 5.2: the first obtains a strip-wide upper bound, while the second transports it to s=-A+it for comparison with a mean-value lower bound.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The balancing idea is explicit in prose, but the displayed definitions of Y, X, the decay factor, and the final exponent at lines 216-258 are severely extraction-damaged. Exact quantitative use requires scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Analytic continuation and endpoint control yield a coefficient-sensitive mean-square lower bound
accepted_units.why_material: Step III quotes a Balasubramanian-Ramachandra theorem whose operational role is to lower-bound a vertical mean square of a Dirichlet series by a weighted sum of squared coefficients, provided analytic continuation, endpoint bounds, and scale conditions hold. The paper then selects the ordinary Dirichlet frequencies needed for its application.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a quoted external result rather than a proof in the source. Only its role in the subsequent argument is safe to retain from this extraction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The theorem's displayed hypotheses and conclusion at lines 263-289 are heavily garbled, including several exponents and indices. Its exact statement is quarantined and requires scan or cited-source verification; no damaged constant is reconstructed here.

accepted_units.title: Goodness converts the mean-value theorem into a large value on the left line
accepted_units.why_material: The authors apply the quoted theorem to the mean square of F(-A+it), using boundary lines supplied by the preceding maximum-modulus work. The coefficient lower bound in goodness guarantees a non-small term in the coefficient sum, which forces a lower bound for the mean square and hence a point where F is large.
accepted_units.context_note: This unit closes the semantic loop begun by the definition: goodness is not merely a label but the precise source of a coefficient contribution that prevents the left-line mean square from being too small.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The direction of the argument is clear from prose at lines 294-305 and 313-328, but the definition of M and the exact H-, A-, and exponential powers in lines 296-327 are extraction-damaged and need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: The propagated upper bound and coefficient-forced lower bound forbid a long pole-free interval
accepted_units.why_material: Step IV compares Lemma 5.3's left-line upper bound with Step III's pointwise lower bound. Choosing the auxiliary constant large forces an upper restriction on H incompatible with H exceeding a constant multiple of the two logarithmic trimming scales, completing the contradiction and Theorem 2.
accepted_units.context_note: The reusable strategic move is the incompatibility of an analytically propagated upper bound with an arithmetically forced lower bound under the no-pole assumption.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The logical comparison and contradiction are stated in prose, but the chained exponential inequality at lines 330-331 has damaged exponents and parameter glyphs; its exact quantitative threshold is scan-dependent.

accepted_units.title: Degree dominance marks the proposed reach of the quotient method
accepted_units.why_material: The concluding remarks propose replacing individual zeta translates by products of ray-class zeta functions or bounded-order derivatives over arbitrary number fields. They identify a comparison between maximal associated field degrees, together with normalization of the denominator at positive infinity, as the kind of condition needed for the method, and flag the need for usable sufficient conditions for goodness.
accepted_units.context_note: This is explicitly presented as forthcoming-work scope and an apparent limit of the method, not as a theorem proved in this paper.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The prose supports the degree-dominance and denominator-normalization ideas. The two product displays and degree inequality at lines 336-345 are damaged, so exact indexing and strictness require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: A distinguished pole in a purely imaginary shift quotient forces recurrent poles nearby
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 3 states a concrete specialization for purely imaginary shifts: if the quotient has the designated pole at s=1 minus the first numerator shift, then it has infinitely many poles above every fixed ordinate and, near each sufficiently large Y, a pole whose ordinate differs from Y by at most a constant times log log Y.
accepted_units.context_note: The theorem is attributed to the forthcoming paper IV. It overlaps immutable v1 unit full_openalex_w963283010_u03 but is retained here only as a fresh v2 depth segment, without changing the v1 record.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The prose gives the pole hypothesis and proximity conclusion, but the product quotient at lines 360-363 is extraction-damaged; the precise arrangement of shifted factors must be verified from the scan.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Contour-to-coefficient contradiction pipeline
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A hypothetical pole-free window permits zero-avoiding horizontal contours; logarithmic-derivative control makes those contours bounded, two decaying-kernel maximum-modulus steps propagate an upper bound to a left line, and a coefficient-sensitive mean-value theorem plus goodness forces an incompatible lower bound there.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This synthesis records the proof architecture only. Exact regions, constants, exponents, and kernel normalizations are unsafe in the normalized text and require scan verification.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Goodness as the arithmetic input to an analytic propagation method
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The analytic hypotheses transport smallness across a rectangle, while goodness supplies a recurrent non-small coefficient that prevents the transported function from remaining too small in mean square; neither side alone yields the contradiction described by the paper.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The precise coefficient interval and lower-bound exponent in the definition are extraction-damaged, so the synthesis is qualitative until the scan is checked.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Structural portability of the pole mechanism
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The text presents the argument as depending on quotient structure, analytic degree balance, and goodness rather than on the Riemann zeta function alone, motivating extensions to derivatives and ordinary, number-field, and ray-class L-functions.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Some extensions are remarks or forthcoming-work claims, and damaged product formulas prevent treating the proposed maximal family as a proved exact classification.

within_source_saturation: All substantive mathematical regions were either represented by accepted units or explicitly quarantined at formula-level spans. Further segmentation would split the same contour, maximum-modulus, or mean-value mechanisms into routine quantitative fragments whose exact content is extraction-unsafe, or would select notation, page furniture, acknowledgements, and bibliography.
stop_reason: The source-specific argument is exhausted after the general pole theorem, its four-step contradiction mechanism, and the concluding extension/specialization are represented; lines 369-429 are non-mathematical end matter, and all earlier omitted displays are identified as extraction-defective rather than silently reconstructed.
